gap: No result ChatGPT got puts a price next to the one-screen limit: a base M1/M2/M3 MacBook Air, a common student laptop, drives only one external display with the lid open (Apple), so the money for a dual or triple extender buys one working added screen without a driver, while the driver-free single 13.3-inch Duex Plus DS costs $183.99 at Mobile Pixels' own store today, below the $195.49 Best Buy price ChatGPT showed.
standout_why: Compared against iTechGuides' '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' (cited) and Macworld's 'Best Portable Monitors for Mac 2026' (cited). TechRepublic, also cited, returned 403 and was not read. iTechGuides lists about 20 products, gives no price for the Duex Plus DS or Duex Max DS, and does not say how many external displays a base MacBook drives; it only says the laptop maker's documentation sets the limit. Macworld says plain M1 and M2 Macs (and the MacBook Neo) are limited to one monitor, but only inside its Trio 3 Pro entry. It does not mention M3, and it gives the Trio as $499.99, which is not today's price. Neither page puts today's maker-store prices next to the one-screen limit, and neither shows that the maker store undercuts Best Buy on the Duex Plus DS.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's lean toward a single screen and makes it firmer for MacBook Air owners. On a base M1, M2 or M3 Air with the lid open, the FOPO S1/S7 and the Trio 3 Pro run one added screen without a driver, so their second panel only works through Mobile Pixels' software (Macworld, Trio) or not at all natively. The pick is a driver-free single 13–14-inch screen. Lowest price paid among the ones read today: Duex Plus DS at $183.99 (Mobile Pixels store, same product page and program as our Duex Max DS). Our Duex Max DS at {after:mobile-pixels-duex-max-ds} wins the segment for a larger 14.1-inch attached screen. The Dell Pro 14 Plus P1425 ($259.99 at Dell, 1.26 lb) is the freestanding choice but costs $76 more than the Duex Plus DS. Our FOPO S1 at {after:fopo-s1-dual-14-inch-laptop-screen-extender} honestly wins two added screens on a budget, but only on Windows laptops or Macs that drive two external displays (based on our record's 'driver-free' note plus Apple's limit).
